title.en: Pitch and gyro-angle to velocity direction

summary: Map one pitch and gyro-angle pair to a unit fast-ion velocity direction in a caller-supplied orthonormal local magnetic frame: sqrt(1-pitch^2)*cos(gyroangle)*a_unit + pitch*b_unit + sqrt(1-pitch^2)*sin(gyroangle)*c_unit.

identity.relation: direction = sqrt(1 - pitch^2) * cos(gyroangle) * a_unit + pitch * b_unit + sqrt(1 - pitch^2) * sin(gyroangle) * c_unit.
identity.direction: pitch + gyro angle + orthonormal local frame (a_unit, b_unit, c_unit) -> one unit velocity direction
identity.definition: The saved FIDASIM pitch_to_vec mapping (framework node N7 fast_ion_fida_response): the pitch fixes the component along b_unit -- the local magnetic-field direction -- (dot(direction, b_unit) == pitch in an exactly-orthonormal frame; within the accepted 1e-12 frame tolerance the identity holds to that tolerance), the gyro angle rotates the perpendicular remainder within the a_unit-c_unit plane, and the output is unit-norm by construction for |pitch| <= 1 in an orthonormal frame. This is a fast-ion diagnostic-frame geometry leaf, not an NBI neutral-beam birth relation.
identity.model: the saved formal implementation, ported verbatim
identity.geometry: one direction; the local frame is caller-supplied
identity.coordinates: pitch and the direction are dimensionless; the gyro angle in radians
identity.boundary: finite pitch in [-1, 1] and finite gyro angle; the frame must be orthonormal (unit norms and pairwise orthogonality within 1e-12)
assumptions: The caller supplies a physically meaningful local frame (e.g. a perpendicular and field-aligned basis at the birth position).
No external physics reference is bound beyond the source closed form.

inputs.name: a_unit
inputs.constraints: Finite; unit norm; orthogonal to the other two.

inputs.name: b_unit
inputs.description: Second orthonormal frame axis (the pitch axis).
inputs.constraints: Finite; unit norm; orthogonal to the other two.

inputs.name: c_unit
inputs.constraints: Finite; unit norm; orthogonal to the other two.

outputs.name: velocity_direction
outputs.constraints: Unit norm for |pitch| <= 1 in an orthonormal frame. dot(direction, b_unit) equals the pitch exactly in an exactly-orthonormal frame; within the accepted 1e-12 frame tolerance the identity holds to that tolerance (a frame with orthogonality error up to 1e-12 shifts the dot product by up to the same order).

preconditions: The caller supplies an orthonormal local magnetic frame at the fast-ion marker position.
supported: Per-particle pitch/gyro-angle to velocity-direction mapping for the fast-ion FIDA response frame geometry.
excluded: Frame construction, pitch/gyro-angle distribution sampling, orbit physics, the FLR position correction (scirel.fusion.first-order-larmor-correction), and NBI neutral-beam birth sampling (energy-component scaling, initial-state materialization, halo and beam-grid sampling live in different framework nodes).

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when any frame vector is non-finite, misshaped, non-unit or non-orthogonal (within 1e-12), when the pitch is outside [-1, 1] or non-finite, or when the gyro angle is non-finite.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Not applicable; the closed form is bounded for accepted inputs.

python.signature: pitch_gyro_to_velocity_direction(*, pitch, gyroangle_rad, a_unit, b_unit, c_unit)

example.description: Map a pitch/gyro pair in the canonical frame and check the unit norm and the pitch-as-b-component identity; pitch = +-1 collapses onto the b axis.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.fusion import pitch_gyro_to_velocity_direction
a = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
b = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
c = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
direction = pitch_gyro_to_velocity_direction(pitch=0.5, gyroangle_rad=np.pi / 3, a_unit=a, b_unit=b, c_unit=c)
assert direction[1] == 0.5
assert abs(np.linalg.norm(direction) - 1.0) < 1e-15
plus = pitch_gyro_to_velocity_direction(pitch=1.0, gyroangle_rad=0.7, a_unit=a, b_unit=b, c_unit=c)
np.testing.assert_allclose(plus, b, atol=1e-15)
try:
    pitch_gyro_to_velocity_direction(pitch=1.5, gyroangle_rad=0.0, a_unit=a, b_unit=b, c_unit=c)
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('a pitch beyond [-1,1] must be rejected')
example.expected: The b-component equals the pitch and the direction is unit-norm; pitch = 1 collapses onto the b axis; a pitch outside [-1, 1] raises ValueError.

scope: Source direction map against independent closed-form recomputation.
Frame orthonormality, pitch domain and failure contracts.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests establish the direction map against independent closed-form recomputation (exact b-component, unit norm within 1e-15 over a pitch/angle sweep), the pitch = +-1 axis collapse independent of the gyro angle, and the fail-closed contracts for non-unit frames, non-orthogonal frames, pitches outside [-1, 1] and non-finite inputs. Environment-gated saved-arm parity is not replayed here; the FIDASIM saved packages ship package-level oracles rather than a pinned source-runtime replay target, and the recorded implementation digest provides the provenance linkage. No test establishes the mapping against an external physics reference beyond the source closed form.
known_limitations: The saved FIDASIM bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only; qualified-L1 delivery root is empty.

The dot(direction, b_unit) == pitch identity is exact only in an exactly-orthonormal frame; the accepted frames are validated to a 1e-12 orthonormality tolerance, so the identity carries that tolerance. The direct tests assert the exact identity only in the canonical frame and the tolerance-bounded identity in random QR frames.
The frame's physical meaning (which axis is field-aligned) is a caller convention; this operator validates orthonormality only.
